subject: Web Development
title: Ten Days That Changed the Web
description: A quick win: understand Ten Days That Changed the Web.

hook.text: In May 1995, Brendan Eich was hired and told to create a new language — in ten days.

buildup.text: Netscape wanted a scripting language that could make web pages interactive.

discovery.text: Eich mixed ideas from Scheme, Self, and Java into a language he called Mocha.

twist.text: The rush left quirks: typeof null returns 'object' — a bug that can never be fixed.

climax.text: That hasty prototype became the foundation for every interactive web page on Earth.

punchline.text: The web's language was built in a sprint.
